caption:
Same URL, different outcome. Follow GET /orders through a configured front door: caller policy, routing, TLS termination and selection of a healthy backend. These are responsibilities that can overlap in one product.

For a failed call, inspect its route, the policy decision and the selected backend. Check TLS on each connection hop.

System Design Crash Course · Lesson 08
#systemdesign #webperformance #beyondlocalhost

takeaway: Trace the path and chosen backend
Inspect the token or policy result
Check TLS on each connection hop

scenes.title: Same URL. Different outcome
scenes.narration: No token: it stops. Valid token: it passes. Your front door checks who is calling.
scenes.note: A configured policy checks the same /orders request.

scenes.title: First, check who is calling
scenes.narration: In this configured example, an API gateway checks the token and rejects the missing-token call before the application.
scenes.note: The missing-token case stops before the application.

scenes.title: Send it to the right service
scenes.narration: With a valid token, the reverse proxy forwards that same orders request to the internal orders service.
scenes.note: The configured route chooses the internal destination.

scenes.title: Where the secure hop ends
scenes.narration: At TLS termination, the edge decrypts HTTPS traffic. Its connection to the backend needs a separate transport-security choice.
scenes.note: This example uses TLS again on the backend hop.

scenes.title: Pick one healthy instance
scenes.narration: A load balancer routes this orders request to one healthy instance, keeping the public endpoint the same for clients.
scenes.note: One request goes to one selected backend, not every backend.

scenes.title: Leave the failed instance out
scenes.narration: If another instance fails its health check, the balancer can exclude it. That does not repair the failed instance.
scenes.note: Health-based selection depends on the configured checks.

scenes.title: One product can do several jobs
scenes.narration: These are responsibilities, not three mandatory products. One configured proxy can handle routing, TLS, and gateway policies together.
scenes.note: The same proxy routes requests and rejects missing-token calls.

scenes.title: Trace your next failed call
scenes.narration: For a failed call, trace its route, inspect the policy result, and confirm which healthy backend received it.
scenes.note: Check the real path instead of guessing from product names.
